repo_notes.content: This wiki is the descriptive source of truth for how this application is currently built: structure, flows, dependencies, contracts and configuration. Document what exists in the code, never what ought to exist, and never imply that something existing is something approved.
repo_notes.author: Agentic SDLC template

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Document the technical profile of this repository: the languages and their versions, the frameworks and major libraries it is built on, the runtime target, the build and package tooling, the top-level directory layout and what each directory holds, and the entry points that start the application. Link each named area to its directory in the source tree.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Document the architectural shape of the system: the services or components it comprises, the responsibility of each, the boundaries between them, and the deployment topology they run in. Include an architecture diagram. Describe the boundaries that exist in the code; do not judge whether they are correct or assess whether a dependency should be allowed.

pages.title: Core Components / Modules
pages.purpose: Document each significant module or package: its responsibility, its public entry points, the other modules it calls, and the modules that call it. Name the directory for each. Cover every top-level source module rather than only the largest ones.

pages.title: Data Flow / Processing Flow
pages.purpose: Document how data moves through the system end to end: entry points (HTTP requests, events, scheduled jobs, batch inputs), the synchronous and asynchronous hops between components, the queues or topics involved, and where data comes to rest. Include a sequence or flow diagram for the primary path, and describe the significant error, retry and compensation paths.

pages.title: Dependencies
pages.purpose: Document what this repository depends on and what depends on it: internal services it calls and the interfaces it exposes to others, external and third-party systems it integrates with, platform services it relies on (databases, caches, message brokers, identity providers), and the notable third-party libraries with the versions pinned in the manifest and lock files. Report versions exactly as found in the code.

pages.title: Storage / Database Layer
pages.purpose: Document the persistent stores this repository owns or reads: each datastore and its purpose, the main entities and their relationships, the schema as defined by migrations or model definitions, the key indexes, and how migrations are applied. Include an entity-relationship diagram where a relational schema exists. Delete this page if the repository has no persistence layer.

pages.title: APIs / Interfaces
pages.purpose: Document every interface this repository exposes and consumes: REST or gRPC endpoints, their request and response shapes, status codes and error model, event and message schemas, and how versioning is implemented. Derive this from the OpenAPI/Swagger, protobuf or schema files in the repository and link to them. Where no specification file exists, derive it from the handler code and state that it was inferred from code.

pages.title: Authentication / Security
pages.purpose: Document the authentication and authorization mechanisms as implemented: how callers are identified, where tokens or sessions are validated, how authorization decisions are made and enforced, and how secrets and cryptographic material are obtained at runtime. Name the middleware, filters or guards involved and link to them. Describe the mechanism only; never include secret values. Delete this page if the repository has no authentication or authorization logic of its own.

pages.title: Deployment / Infrastructure
pages.purpose: Document how this repository is built, packaged and deployed: the CI/CD pipeline stages, the container or artifact build, the environments it deploys to, the infrastructure-as-code that defines its runtime, and the health, readiness and observability hooks it exposes. Derive this from the pipeline definitions, Dockerfiles and IaC present in the repository. Delete this page if deployment is defined entirely outside this repository.

pages.title: Configuration
pages.purpose: Document how this application is configured: the configuration files and their precedence, the environment variables and what each one controls, feature flags and their defaults, and which settings differ between environments. List configuration keys by name with their purpose and default, never their real values.

pages.title: Unit Testing
pages.purpose: Document the test suites present in this repository: the frameworks and runners in use, where tests live and how they are named, how fixtures, mocks and test data are provided, and the commands that execute them. Describe testing as it exists. Coverage thresholds and mandatory test types are policy and belong to the knowledge-testing skill, not this page. Delete this page if the repository has no meaningful test suite yet.
